# C2 — Deployment timing

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | **UNRESOLVED** — An open question, conflict, or missing measurement blocks a stronger statement. |
| Strongest accepted evidence | IMPLEMENTATION ONLY |
| Evidence classes cited | IMPLEMENTATION, SYNTHETIC, TEST PROCEDURE |
| Gate reached | SYNTHETIC TEST (next: INERT BENCH SETUP) |
| Last review | CURRENT — snapshot recorded 2026-09-28 by tooling snapshot (no human review) |

**Question.** Does the hardware-timed deploy output fire at the requested delay with sub-millisecond jitter, without blocking the control loop?

**Current statement.** Firmware schedules the deploy output with a one-shot esp_timer at a requested 50 ms delay. No hardware timing has been measured; the only timing data is a 21-row synthetic fixture that exercises report arithmetic.

| R-C2-NONBLOCKING | Scheduling the deployment does not block the control loop. | human review | none stated | judgement, not a value | REQUIRES HUMAN REVIEW |

## Known contradictions

## Open questions

- No hardware timing capture exists.

## Discrepancies

- [D-017](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-017) (OPEN) Ignition requires deployed fins, but deployment requires a boost-level acceleration
- [D-018](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-018) (OPEN) Live telemetry timestamps are launcher relay times, not rocket sample times
- [D-024](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-024) (OPEN) The deploy bench sketch measures a timer with the same timer
- [D-016](../DISCREPANCIES.md#d-016) (RESOLVED) Architecture diagram omitted the rocket's fins-deployed ignition gate

## Assumptions

- The requested delay in firmware is the intended deployment delay.
- Jitter means the spread of output-edge time relative to the trigger, measured by an instrument independent of the ESP32 clock.

## Limitations

- Synthetic values do not demonstrate timer, scheduler, or actuator behavior.
- Twenty-one rows cannot bound a tail latency even if they were real.
- The existing bench sketch times the callback with the clock it is measuring (D-024).

## Measurement needed to close the next gate

- Inert GPIO 33 edge timing against an external trigger reference, per proposed pre-registration P-001.

## Pre-registered experiments

- P-001 (proposed)

## What this claim does not establish

- Any inert physical measurement: none has been accepted for this claim.
- Physical performance of any hardware.
- Flight readiness or safety for live propulsion.
